note: Example exports for software, UI, and analysis development.

datasets.acquisition_path: phyphox phone light sensor
datasets.scenario: Same reference/sample/dark sequence as the SensorTag run, recorded on a phone.
realism: Phone light sensors are model-dependent; this trace assumes a 10 Hz sensor with 2% noise.
The values differ from the SensorTag run because the optical gain and spectral weighting differ.
Time jitter is small but nonzero because the phone supplies sensor timestamps.
The two files are alternative runs, not simultaneous measurements.

datasets.acquisition_path: SensorTag BLE AA71 notification, AA73=0x50 (0.8 s)
datasets.scenario: Covered sensor, white reference tile, grey sample, black sample, then covered again; the lamp is left running throughout.
realism: Exact OPT3001 exponent/mantissa encoding; the exported value is decoded from the raw word.
0.01 lx resolution at the lowest range, automatic range selection, 3% gain error, and 1% noise.
The XML reconstructs time as 0.8 s times the sample count, not from packet timestamps.
The built-in contrast (max-min)/max is an extrema statistic, not a calibrated albedo.
datasets.notes: The trailing raw word is not part of the phyphox export; it is provided for decoder checks.

datasets.acquisition_path: SensorTag BLE AA41 notification, AA44=0x64 (1 s)
datasets.scenario: Open and covered vessels start at 22 °C, a lamp is switched on at 60 s, and both cool after 360 s; the covered vessel rises faster and higher.
realism: The XML uses the BMP280 die-temperature word, not the HDC1000 air sensor; a self-heating offset is included.
Signed 24-bit temperature word with 0.01 °C scaling, as in the experiment.
The covered vessel has a larger asymptote and a shorter time constant than the open vessel.
Time is reconstructed from the first tag's sample count at 1 s per sample.
The two tags have different offsets and noise, so the difference is not a clean physical contrast.
datasets.notes: The trailing raw words are not exported by the XML; they let the decoder be checked.

datasets.sensor: TI TMP007 infrared thermopile (SensorTag) and Bluetooth HID mouse
datasets.acquisition_path: SensorTag AA01 notification, AA03=0x1E (0.3 s), plus BLE HID mouse
datasets.scenario: A warm target and SensorTag move together on a rail from 0.15 m to 0.80 m and back; the apparent IR temperature settles at each stop.
realism: TMP007 conversion time is 0.25 s; the file samples at 0.3 s and includes a 1.4 s thermal lag.
Object temperature word is 0.03125 °C resolution; the die word is the ambient channel.
Mouse distance uses about 0.0002 m/count, with a small slip event near 60 samples.
The unsigned XML conversion requires nonnegative temperatures; this run stays above 20 °C.
The file has no export timestamp in the XML; Time (s) is added here for readability.
datasets.notes: d (a.u.) is accumulated mouse counts, not metres. Divide by 5000 for an approximate metre reading after calibration.

datasets.acquisition_path: phyphox phone pressure sensor
datasets.scenario: The same chamber pressure profile recorded on a phone barometer.
realism: Phone barometers are model-dependent; this trace assumes 10 Hz, 0.01 hPa resolution, and 0.015 hPa noise.
A -0.3 hPa offset and a slightly different noise level distinguish it from the SensorTag run.
Phone timestamps have small arrival jitter.
The two files are alternative runs, not simultaneous measurements.

datasets.acquisition_path: SensorTag BLE AA41 notification, AA44=0x0A (0.1 s)
datasets.scenario: Near-ambient baseline, pump to +35 hPa, a slow 1.5 hPa leak over 30 s, release, and a final baseline.
realism: BMP280 range is 300-1100 hPa; the 35 hPa excursion remains inside it.
Pressure word is 0.01 hPa resolution, with +0.6 hPa offset and 0.02 hPa noise.
A 0.35 s port/equilibration lag is applied to the chamber step.
The XML reconstructs time as 0.1 s times the sample count.
The auxiliary temperature word is included as a raw column even though the XML does not export it.
datasets.notes: This is a classroom chamber run, not a Martian pressure measurement.

datasets.sensor: Owon B35T digital multimeter, DC voltage
datasets.acquisition_path: Owon BDM BLE notification, characteristic FFF4
datasets.scenario: A DC calibration staircase: 0 V, 1 V, 1.5 V, 2 V, -1 V, and 0.5 V, each held for about 10 s.
realism: The Owon B35T updates digital data 3 times/s on the meter and about 2 times/s in the app.
The 6 V DC range has 1 mV resolution; a 0.2% gain error, 0.4 mV offset, and 0.3 mV noise are included.
Raw fields follow the B35T branch of the supplied decoder: 5-character numeric field, decimal code 1, unit code 0.
The debug XML exports only Time (s) and y; the raw fields are extra columns for decoder testing.
The analysis sleep of 0.05 s is not a 20 Hz acquisition rate.
datasets.notes: The positive and negative steps exercise the decoder's sign handling.

datasets.sensor: Bosch BMP280 pressure and die temperature (SensorTag)
datasets.acquisition_path: SensorTag BLE AA41 notification, AA44=0x64 (1 s)
datasets.scenario: A slow 7% volume reduction raises pressure by about 75 hPa and warms the barometer die by about 1.4 °C, followed by a release.
realism: Pressure is the compensated BMP280 absolute value, scaled by 0.01 hPa.
Temperature is the barometer die temperature, not an independent gas thermometer.
The compression is slow enough to be nearly isothermal; the die warming is mostly self-heating and work.
Reconstructed time is 1 s per sample and is exported in minutes.
A +0.55 hPa and +0.40 °C offset plus 0.02 hPa and 0.015 °C noise are included.
datasets.notes: The 1081 hPa peak stays inside the BMP280 300-1100 hPa rated interval. The scenario is illustrative, not a validated chamber run.

datasets.acquisition_path: SensorTag BLE AA41 notification, AA44=0x64 (1 s)
datasets.scenario: Day-side and night-side model regions; the lamp is on from 30 s to 210 s, then both sides cool.
realism: Both columns are BMP280 die temperatures, not validated surface or air temperatures.
The day side has a larger rise and a faster initial response; the night side stays nearly flat.
Offsets differ between tags and 0.01 °C quantisation/noise is included.
Time is reconstructed from tag 1's sample count for both columns.

datasets.sensor: TI OPT3001 ambient light sensor (two SensorTags)
datasets.acquisition_path: SensorTag BLE AA71 notification, AA73=0x50 (0.8 s)
datasets.scenario: Day-side illuminance near 12,000 lx and night-side stray light near 28 lx, lamp on 30-210 s.
realism: OPT3001 automatic range selection and 0.01 lx encoding; the raw words are exported here for traceability.
The 12,000 lx day side and 28 lx night side differ by more than two orders of magnitude.
A 3% gain error, 0.8% noise, and a slow lamp ripple are included.
The XML labels both light columns identically; this file suffixes them 1 and 2 for readability.

datasets.acquisition_path: SensorTag BLE AA01 notification, AA03=0x1E (0.3 s)
datasets.scenario: The same day/night illumination cycle seen by two TMP007 channels.
realism: Object and ambient/die temperature words use 0.03125 °C resolution.
The object channel includes a 1 °C offset and 0.08 °C noise; the die channel is smoother.
The day-side object temperature rises by about 22 °C under the lamp; the night side stays near ambient.
The XML's unsigned conversion is valid here because all temperatures are positive.
datasets.notes: The trailing raw words are extra columns; the XML exports the four converted temperatures.

datasets.sensor: Solar cell through an Owon B35T digital multimeter
datasets.acquisition_path: Owon BDM BLE notification, characteristic FFF4
datasets.scenario: The same three-transit sequence seen as a 1.85 V solar-cell signal with 4% dips.
realism: The Owon app path updates about twice per second, so a 4 s transit contains only about 8 samples.
The solar-cell voltage is assumed to be in a linear operating region; real open-circuit cells are logarithmic.
1 mV quantisation, 0.2% gain error, 0.4 mV offset, and 0.4 mV noise are included.
The raw fields follow the B35T decoder branch used by the experiment.
The XML exports this path as a relative signal in volts, not as a normalized light curve.
datasets.notes: This path demonstrates why transducer linearity and meter range are part of the measurement model.

datasets.acquisition_path: phyphox phone light sensor
datasets.scenario: The same three-transit sequence recorded at 10 Hz on a phone.
realism: The 10 Hz cadence resolves the 4 s events with about 40 samples each.
A 0.15% noise level and small timestamp jitter are included.
The baseline differs from the SensorTag run because the phone's optical gain and spectral response differ.
The file is an alternative acquisition path, not a simultaneous measurement.

datasets.acquisition_path: SensorTag BLE AA71 notification, AA73=0x50 (0.8 s)
datasets.scenario: Three 4% transits of 4 s duration at 22 s, 52 s, and 82 s, with a stable 850 lx baseline.
realism: Transit depth is 4.0%, with 0.8 s ingress/egress, comparable to the sampling interval.
The 0.8 s cadence gives only about 5 samples per transit, so the event is intentionally undersampled.
A 0.2% noise level and slow lamp drift are included.
The XML reconstructs time as 0.8 s times the sample count.
The trailing raw word is provided for decoder checks, not by the XML export.
datasets.notes: The event centres and duration are chosen so the built-in threshold logic can find six on/off transitions.

datasets.acquisition_path: Nano 33 BLE Sense -> BLE notification (mode 1)
datasets.scenario: Board resting flat, tilted ±30 degrees, picked up and shaken, tapped three times, then rolled 90 degrees and returned flat.
realism: Firmware sends acceleration in g; phyphox multiplies by 9.81 for the m/s² columns.
±4 g selected by the pinned Arduino_LSM9DS1 library; 16-bit LSB = 4/32768 g.
119 Hz internal rate is decimated to a 20 Hz notification stream.
Magnitude is computed from the transmitted components, not added independently.
Small zero-g offsets, 1/f drift, broadband noise, and a 7.5 Hz ring-down are included.
datasets.notes: The timestamp advances in 50 ms or 51 ms steps, matching millis()-driven scheduling.

datasets.acquisition_path: Nano 33 BLE Sense -> BLE notification (mode 9)
datasets.scenario: A0 potentiometer sweep, A1 light-dependent-resistor step, and A2 RC charge/discharge with tau = 1 s.
realism: Default 10-bit codes 0-1023; phyphox multiplies by 3.226 mV/count.
Actual reference 3.31 V and per-channel gain/offset errors make the displayed mV slightly wrong.
Counts are integers and clip at the ADC rails.
A2 includes 50 Hz mains pickup, which aliases at the 20 Hz sampling rate.
A0, A1, and A2 are converted sequentially; there is no simultaneous-sample guarantee.
datasets.notes: The RC curve is sampled about 20 times per time constant, so the shape is resolved but not oversampled.

datasets.acquisition_path: Nano 33 BLE Sense -> BLE notification (mode 2)
datasets.scenario: Stationary baseline, ±45 deg/s yaw plateaus, +60 deg/s roll, -35 deg/s pitch, then stationary again.
realism: Firmware sends deg/s; phyphox multiplies by pi/180 for the rad/s columns.
±2000 deg/s range; 16-bit LSB = 2000/32768 deg/s = 0.061035 deg/s.
The library-to-datasheet scale ratio 0.87193 is applied, so a true 45 deg/s plateau reads about 39.2 deg/s.
Zero-rate bias, 1/f drift, 0.06 deg/s broadband noise, and hand tremor are included.
Magnitude is computed from the three transmitted components.
datasets.notes: A stationary board still reports a small nonzero rate; the bias is not removed.

datasets.acquisition_path: Nano 33 BLE Sense -> BLE notification (mode 6)
datasets.scenario: Dim room, warm white lamp, red/green/blue cards, a saturated phone flashlight, then dim room again.
realism: Raw 16-bit RGBC counts, not lux; phyphox displays arbitrary units.
The library's 4-cycle integration gives a nominal 4100-count saturation, not 65535.
Channel gains, dark counts, shot-like noise, and a 3.7 Hz lamp ripple are included.
Clear is generally larger than each colour channel; all channels clip at 4100.
The 11.12 ms integration is much shorter than the 50 ms notification interval.
datasets.notes: Counts are integers, matching the sensor registers and the firmware's int-to-float cast.

datasets.acquisition_path: Nano 33 BLE Sense -> BLE notification (mode 3)
datasets.scenario: Earth-field baseline, 80 degree yaw, 25 degree tilt, a magnet approach near 30 s, then return to the starting orientation.
realism: ±4 gauss range = ±400 µT; 16-bit LSB = 400/32768 µT = 0.012207 µT.
The library-to-datasheet scale ratio 0.87193 is applied, so the uncalibrated magnitude reads low.
Earth field is about 48.3 µT total in Cologne; hard-iron and soft-iron terms shift the components.
Four NaN rows represent magneticFieldAvailable() returning false at the 20 Hz frame boundary.
Magnitude is computed from the transmitted components, including the disturbed interval.
datasets.notes: µT values are sensor-frame components; they are not a calibrated compass heading.

datasets.acquisition_path: Nano 33 BLE Sense -> BLE notification (mode 4)
datasets.scenario: Indoor baseline near 1009 hPa, a 1.2 m lift, a 3 m stair climb, a sealed-bag squeeze near 120 s, and slow room drift.
realism: Firmware sends kPa; phyphox multiplies by 10 for the hPa column.
24-bit output with 4096 LSB/hPa, i.e. 0.000244 hPa per code.
A +0.55 hPa uncalibrated offset, 0.02 hPa noise, and 30 s drift are included.
Pressure follows a 0.8 s port/equilibration lag rather than the height step instantly.
A 1.2 m lift changes pressure by about 0.144 hPa; 3 m by about 0.36 hPa.
datasets.notes: The 8 hPa bag excursion stays well inside the 260-1260 hPa sensor range.

datasets.sensor: ST HTS221 temperature and humidity sensor
datasets.acquisition_path: Nano 33 BLE Sense -> BLE notification (mode 5)
datasets.scenario: Powered-board warm-up, two breath events, and a lamp/hand warming interval that raises temperature and lowers relative humidity.
realism: Humidity is derived from a conserved vapour pressure and the Magnus saturation curve, so it falls when temperature rises.
A 15 s temperature lag and a 10 s humidity lag follow the HTS221 response times.
Typical offsets (+0.32 °C, +1.7 %RH), 0.016 °C and 0.004 %RH quantisation, and 1/f drift are included.
The firmware reads temperature first and humidity second; the two numbers are not simultaneous conversions.
The board self-heating term is separate from the air-temperature changes.
datasets.notes: Relative humidity is a percentage, not a fraction; 45 %RH is written 45.0 here.
